songInfo.title: Am I Ever Gonna See Your Face Again

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: A Mixolydian / A Major driving with open A pedal tone and classic ♭VII (G) and IV (D) rock cadences

scalesUsed.name: A Major Pentatonic
scalesUsed.application: Delivers the sweet, melodic intro guitar phrasing and classical-influenced lead hooks

scalesUsed.name: A Mixolydian
scalesUsed.notes: A - B - C# - D - E - F# - G
scalesUsed.application: Drives the iconic A - G/A - D/A intro riff and thunderous power chord chorus

scalesUsed.name: A Minor Pentatonic
scalesUsed.application: Supplies the raw blues-rock bite and vocal-responding fills in the high-energy bridge and solo

mainProgression.description: The quintessential Australian pub rock progression built on an open A pedal bass note supporting ringing triads

sectionProgressions.description: Sparkling clean pedal-point progression letting the open 5th string ring underneath moving chord voicings

sectionProgressions.progression: A - G/A - D/A - A - Bm - D - E
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: I - ♭VII - IV - I - ii - IV - V
sectionProgressions.description: Gentle acoustic-style clean groove building through minor second to dominant turnaround
Full-throttle overdriven power chords propelling the crowd-roaring Australian call-and-response anthem

harmonicFunction: A (Tonic I): Welcoming home key established with warm open string resonance
G/A (Subtonic ♭VII): Injects the signature Mixolydian pub-rock flavor over the persistent A pedal tone
D/A (Subdominant IV): Uplifting classic resolution stepping smoothly back to the tonic A
E (Dominant V): Builds the pre-chorus tension that launches the explosive chorus entry

techniques.name: Pedal Tone Chord Strumming
techniques.description: Maintaining a continuous ringing open A string while shifting upper triad shapes across the neck

notes: Keep the open 5th string vibrating freely without accidental finger damping
Use the index, middle, and ring fingers to articulate the upper chord shapes on strings 2, 3, and 4
Strum with an even, shimmering dynamic balance

techniques.name: Pub-Rock Crowd Dynamics
techniques.description: Controlling the stark contrast between delicate storytelling verses and roof-raising chorus anthems

notes: Keep verses sparse, clean, and conversational with light pick touch
Explode into the chorus with full-body downstrokes on heavy bridge pickup crunch
Leave space for the audience response chants between chorus measures

sections.name: Timeless Clean Chime Intro
sections.description: One of the most famous openings in Australian music, featuring sparkling clean triads over a droning open A string
notes: Hold the open 5th string (A) down as a continuous acoustic pedal tone
Shape the G triad cleanly on the D, G, and B strings
Let the final A major chord ring with sparkling chime

sections.name: Driving Verse Strum & Rhythm
sections.description: A rhythmic progression through A, G/A, D/A, climbing into Bm and E for the pre-chorus lift
sections.progression: A - G/A - D/A - A - Bm - E
notes: Maintain a steady, swinging eighth-note right-hand rhythm
Barre the 2nd fret cleanly for the Bm chord transition
Crescendo through the E major chord to prepare for the thunderous chorus

sections.name: Anthemic Overdriven Chorus
sections.description: The immortal pub rock chorus roaring with cranked Marshall power chords and timeless Australian energy
notes: Slam into the A5 power chord with authoritative right-hand force
Execute rapid changes to G5 and D5 with clean string dampening
Hold the final A5 chord for two full measures of singing sustain

sections.name: Classical-Rock Melodic Solo
sections.description: Rick Brewster's classically influenced guitar solo showcasing lyrical phrasing, precise bends, and sweet vibrato
notes: Begin with lyrical scalar steps on the G and B strings
Target the C# chord tone (9th fret E string) on the change to A major
End with a soaring high E bend at the 14th fret resolving gracefully

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster or Gibson SG Standard
guitar.pickup: Neck/middle pickup for sparkling intro chiming; bridge pickup for roaring chorus crunch

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP 50W Super Lead into 4x12 cabinet with Celestion speakers

effects.distortion: Natural Marshall tube crunch boosted with an analog clean boost
effects.other: Albert Studios compression on the intro acoustic/clean guitar tracks

beginner.title: Open Chords & The A Pedal Note
steps: Learn the A, G/A, and D/A triad shapes keeping the open 5th string ringing
Master the basic A-G-D chorus power chord changes

intermediate.title: Full Song Arrangement & Dynamics
steps: Transition seamlessly between clean intro chiming and roaring chorus crunch
Incorporate the Bm barre chord in the verse progression
Lock into the 128 BPM groove with consistent rhythm feel

advanced.title: Rick Brewster Melodic Soloing
steps: Learn the complete guitar solo focusing on target chord tones
Master the 14th fret bends and singing vibrato control
Capture the authentic Australian pub rock live swagger

commonMistakes: Muting the open A string accidentally during the intro triads
Playing the chorus with too much preamp distortion, muddying the chord definition
Over-bending the 14th fret note in the lead solo
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: A pedal tone triad positioning warm-up
10 mins: Slow metronome drill on the intro triad shifts at 95 BPM
10 mins: Power chord chorus transitions and dynamic switches at 115 BPM
5 mins: Full track playthrough at 128 BPM performance speed
focusAreas: Ringing open A string sustain during chord changes
Dynamic impact when exploding into the chorus power chords
Vibrato control on sustained solo notes
metronomeWork: Start at 90 BPM ensuring all three intro triad strings ring with equal volume
Advance to 110 BPM coordinating right-hand strumming dynamics
Perform at full 128 BPM locking in with the driving rock tempo
